races.paceDynamic: Hello Luna will take them along at a solid tempo with Secret Handsheikh, Honour Your Dreams and several other prominent types pressing close behind, creating a genuine pace through the early stages. The substantial group of prominent runners (Hello Luna, Honour Your Dreams, Secret Handsheikh, Under Curfew, Barnsnape Boy, Cameley Days, Tilsworth Ony Ta) will ensure no soft lead scenario develops. With hold-up horses Cabeza De Llave, Dragon God, Manhattan Chute and She Went Whoosh having plenty to find from the rear in a sprint, this pace dynamic clearly favours prominent racers who can secure good early positions without getting embroiled in destructive speed battles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Luna and the prominent brigade maintain strong gallop without over-racing
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will find out the hold-up horses over this minimum trip, while those handy to the pace can kick clear in the final furlong. Horses like Honour Your Dreams and Secret Handsheikh are perfectly positioned to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group goes too fast early and tie up in the final stages
scenarios.body: The strong early tempo will set up a perfect storm for closers to sweep up late, particularly those with tactical speed. Dragon God and Cabeza De Llave can exploit tired leaders with their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hello Luna Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Luna gets an easy lead and sustains her effort to the line
scenarios.body: The mare can dictate terms from the front and prove too tough to peg back, especially with her solid recent form at this trip. Her prominent style could translate to outright leadership if others are reluctant to press.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Outsider Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly unsustainable and eliminates the fancied runners
scenarios.body: A lightly-raced improver like Manhattan Chute or returning Barnsnape Boy could capitalize on a chaotic finish where form horses disappoint. The extreme pace scenario opens doors for unconsidered contenders.

watchPoints.text: Cameley Days dropped out tamely at Leicester 12 days ago and may repeat her fade-in-finish pattern
Under Curfew returns from 84-day absence which could blunt the 10-year-old's finishing kick significantly
Barnsnape Boy faces fitness questions after 203-day layoff despite encouraging past form in these conditions
Dragon God's closing style could be perfectly timed if the prominent brigade over-exerts early
Secret Handsheikh's return to turf from artificial surfaces should aid his chances considerably

races.paceDynamic: Jazl emerges as the only confirmed front-runner in this small field, with his prominent style likely to see him dictate terms from the rail. The lack of other pace pressers means Jazl can set sustainable fractions without being hassled early, while the prominent quartet of Starryfield, Swiped, and Stolen will track behind. Miss Nightcap's unraced status makes her positioning unknown, but the overall setup creates a scenario where the pace will be honest but not punishing. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed, as they can position perfectly behind an uncontested leader and have first run when the race develops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jazl Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Jazl translates his early pace advantage into sustainable sectionals without pressure
scenarios.body: His front-running style maximizes the benefit of an uncontested lead, while the lack of early speed from others allows him to dictate ideal fractions for his finishing kick. The prominent pack arrives too late as Jazl has saved enough for the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the tracking group of prominent runners can position perfectly behind Jazl's honest pace
scenarios.body: Starryfield and Swiped benefit from the perfect tow as Jazl softens up the ground, allowing their superior ratings to tell in a well-run race. The tactical positioning proves decisive in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newcomer Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Nightcap's breeding and 40k price tag translates into immediate ability on debut
scenarios.body: Her unknown quantity status masks genuine talent, and she benefits from settling behind the established pace before unleashing a telling finish. The maiden field proves weaker than her natural ability level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Jazl's long absence tells and he stops quickly after setting the fractions
scenarios.body: The front-runner's stamina gives way in the final 100 yards, creating a scramble where any of the prominent runners can capitalize. Stolen's recent run gives her the fitness edge in a slowly-run finish.

watchPoints.text: Jazl's fitness after 248 days could see him weaken dramatically in final furlong if the break has affected his stamina base.
Miss Nightcap's debut positioning will reveal much about her ability level and whether the breeding translates to immediate racecourse talent.
Starryfield's early positioning behind Jazl determines if he can utilize his best form figures at this distance.
Swiped's seasonal return after 270 days and gelding operation creates unknown fitness and behavioral factors.
The pace through halfway sectionals will show if Jazl can maintain his kick or if prominent runners can time their challenge perfectly.

races.paceDynamic: Dutch Kingdom holds a monopoly on early pace with five horses (Zarathos, The Hare Rail, Kodi Fire, Norflondonforever, Canopus) all wanting prominent positions behind him. This creates inevitable congestion in the first quarter-mile as they jostle for tactical spots, with pressure building through the middle stages as the field compresses. The solo leader Dutch Kingdom can dictate terms unchallenged while those packed behind face traffic problems turning for home. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can bypass the prominent-runner scrum and finish with clear runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack creates the expected traffic jam 2-3 furlongs out
scenarios.body: Dutch Kingdom's soft lead gets swallowed as hold-up horses sweep past the stalled prominent runners with clear passages. The backmarkers benefit from others' positional mistakes and superior finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent horse (Zarathos/Kodi Fire) secures the ideal second position and avoids trouble
scenarios.body: They can track Dutch Kingdom's steady gallop and kick clear of the pack when it matters, capitalizing on tactical positioning. The leader and second have established crucial gaps over the struggling field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dutch Kingdom Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the lone leader gets uncontested fractions and the prominent pack eliminates each other
scenarios.body: Dutch Kingdom exploits his tactical advantage to build an unassailable lead while others fight for scraps behind. His stamina holds against late challengers who've used too much energy in traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Dutch Kingdom goes too slow early and all prominent runners ease off the gas
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole with no true pace throughout the contest. This nullifies tactical advantages and creates a lottery finish from a bunched field.

watchPoints.text: Dutch Kingdom must improve significantly from his yard debut flop or the pace advantage becomes meaningless
Zarathos and Kodi Fire clash for the crucial second position early, winner likely avoids this battle

Norflondonforever headgear removal after 387-day break creates multiple unknowns in combination

races.paceDynamic: Koko Blue is the sole confirmed front runner and will control this contest from the start, likely establishing a comfortable lead with Douglas Dc and Gearing's Point tracking in prominent positions. With no pace pressure, Koko Blue can dictate a measured gallop over this stamina-testing 1m3½f trip, though her tendency to fade late is a concern. The large contingent of hold-up horses including Moon Over The Sea, Belle Amie, Stintino Sunset, and Fullforward will be relying on the leaders softening each other up. This tactical scenario clearly favours the prominent runners who can position close enough to strike without getting caught up in a late cavalry charge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Benefits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Koko Blue maintains a steady gallop without folding
scenarios.body: The measured tempo allows prominent runners to stay in touch and maintain their kick, while hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on good going. Gearing's Point and Douglas Dc benefit most from tracking the lone leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Cavalry Charge
scenarios.trigger: If Koko Blue's tendency to fade manifests over this longer trip
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade gets the perfect setup as the leaders tire, allowing the strongest stayers to sweep past in the final furlong. Moon Over The Sea's recent Bath win and Belle Amie's Wolverhampton success show they can capitalize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Koko Blue improves for the stable switch and gets the trip
scenarios.body: The Tom Clover newcomer benefits from the lack of early pace pressure and finds enough stamina to see off late challengers on this good ground. Her prominent positioning becomes decisive when others are too far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a tactical crawl that transforms into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows unconsidered horses with turn of foot to get into contention, particularly those with recent form who've been underestimated by the market. Fullforward's recent Lingfield run suggests readiness.

runners_data.spotlight: All three of his wins have come at Brighton; well treated on last summer's ready 1m2f win but returning from an absence perhaps not the time to catch him.

runners_data.name: Haveagobeau
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who took 31 attempts to break maiden; recent Lingfield win gives confidence but apprentice jockey a concern
runners_data.comment: Two wins and two seconds from his last five starts; not fully exposed over 1m2f
runners_data.spotlight: Took an age to get off the mark, finally opening his account at the 31st attempt in a 1m2f handicap at Lingfield (AW) in January; four runs since, twice finishing second before recording another Lingfield success six weeks ago; still unexposed at this trip and he is effective on turf.

runners_data.name: Read All About It
runners_data.note: Front-running mare who returned to form with cheekpieces last time; 79 days off the track but showed promise in that comeback
runners_data.comment: Back to form in first-time cheekpieces in February (9.4f); good chance if building on it
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden; returned to form when third of eight in a Wolverhampton handicap in February (9.4f; cheekpieces first time); still has time to deliver on her early promise and neither track nor ground should be an issue; shortlisted.

races.paceDynamic: Read All About It and Hawaiian King will dispute the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to engage from the start. The small field of eight means little pressure behind the leaders, allowing them to dictate a controlled gallop through the middle sections. With most others holding up (Happy Chandler, Celebrating Ethel, Fighting Poet, Haveagobeau), the pace could become tactical in the closing stages. This setup strongly favours the hold-up horses who can finish fast off what may become a modest early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too slow early and set up a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The pace will collapse in the final three furlongs as multiple hold-up horses unleash simultaneously. Happy Chandler's recent winning form at the trip and Celebrating Ethel's staying power will prove decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Beta Reader and Bizou position perfectly behind the battling leaders
scenarios.body: They can track the pace without getting involved in early speed duels, then strike when the front-runners weaken. Beta Reader's turf promise and Bizou's seasonal return form make them dangerous.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one leader gets first run while the other ties up
scenarios.body: The survivor will have enough left to hold off the late charge from a tactical race. Read All About It's recent return to form gives her the edge over Hawaiian King's turf concerns.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go extremely conservatively and create a cavalry charge
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the two-furlong pole with little between them. Any of the hold-up horses could emerge from the pack finish.

Fighting Poet faces a steep task returning from a 192-day layoff against race-fit opponents
Happy Chandler carries a 5lb penalty for his recent Leicester win but that victory came at this exact distance
Both Beta Reader and Bizou return from 5-6 week breaks which could either freshen them or leave them short of peak fitness
The small field means little early pressure which could set up a messy tactical finish favoring those with the best turn of foot

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (Brighton Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: May Encounter
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but 212 days off and poor trainer form creates doubt about readiness

runners_data.name: Capote's Dream
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner but last victory was August 2023 and recent AW form disappointing
runners_data.comment: Three-time C&D winner; out of sorts on AW when last seen; now drops to Class 6
runners_data.spotlight: Three of his wins have come over C&D but the last victory was back in August 2023; out of sorts on AW over the winter but he drops into a Class 6 and if he is to stage a revival, it is likely to be here.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with recent near-misses, better on AW than turf but drops to lowest grade
runners_data.comment: Exposed 16-race maiden but she looks capable of winning a small race; perhaps not this one
runners_data.spotlight: 0-16 but she has had some near misses along the way, notably at Wolverhampton in February (6f) when beaten a nose by a thriving rival; not so good back on turf at Leicester 12 days ago; may have to wait longer to shed her maiden tag.

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: Previous course winner back to winning mark but trainer 0-14 in last fortnight raises concerns
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; on a good mark and capable of going well if the ground is no issue
runners_data.spotlight: Two turf wins last summer, including C&D, and she added a 7f handicap at Kempton to her tally in February; back to a winning mark and can't be discounted, but fast ground is a slight concern.

runners_data.name: Candy Warhol
runners_data.note: Front-runner with recent seconds over shorter trip, unproven on turf but handles good to firm
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who arrives in form; 0-8 on turf and not sure to benefit from return to 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; arrives on the back of two second-place finishes over 5f on the AW; 0-8 on turf but is effective on good to firm; not sure to benefit from the return to 6f.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Moon
runners_data.note: Four AW wins but struggled on turf including as beaten favourite last time out
runners_data.comment: 4 AW wins but not shown comparable form on turf; still has time to get it right on grass
runners_data.spotlight: Four AW wins to her name but she is yet to show comparable form on turf, including when a beaten favourite at Nottingham 11 days ago; may come good on the grass at some point.

runners_data.name: My Mate Kev
runners_data.note: Now 9lb lower than last win but unlikely to get easy lead with Midnight Call present
runners_data.comment: 9lb lower than for Newmarket win last May but there has been little to shout about since
runners_data.spotlight: Now 9lb lower than for his Newmarket win last May (6f, good); little to shout about since and unlikely to get an easy time of things up front.

runners_data.name: Just Jump
runners_data.note: Slow starts recurring theme but shaped well on stable debut, needs luck from hold-up position
runners_data.comment: Has the ability to defy this mark but he's an habitual slow starter and he'll need luck
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped well when third at Lingfield (6f, AW) on his stable debut in February; hasn't fared so well since, with slow starts a recurring theme, and he will need luck in running if he blows the start from stall 1; cheekpieces the headgear of choice today.

runners_data.name: Midnight Call
runners_data.note: Natural leader with five recent AW wins but failed off this mark 16 days ago
runners_data.comment: Five Wolverhampton wins since November; handicapper may now have caught up
runners_data.spotlight: Promise on turf last summer and she has made good progress on AW since November, winning five times at Wolverhampton; came up short off this mark 16 days ago and the handicapper may now have her measure.

runners_data.name: Margorie
runners_data.note: One soft ground win but no handicap impact, cheekpieces tried last time showed slight improvement
runners_data.comment: Shock C&D win last September came on soft ground; little impact in handicaps since
runners_data.spotlight: Sprung a surprise in a soft-ground C&D maiden last September; no impact in handicaps and although last time at Haydock (cheekpieces first time) was a bit better, others are more appealing.

runners_data.name: Dreambird Dolly
runners_data.note: Exposed maiden returning from 189-day break with little chance against these
runners_data.comment: Exposed 16-race maiden; absent for six months and easy enough to look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed 16-race maiden; returns from six months off and others have much more pressing claims.

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Call and Candy Warhol will set the early tempo, with both having prominent/leading tendencies and recent form suggesting they'll go forward from the start. The pace should be steady rather than frantic with only these two likely to press early, creating a sustainable gallop that won't collapse in the final furlong. Dreambird Dolly may also track close but lacks recent match fitness after 189 days off. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish late, as the lack of early pace pressure will leave plenty in reserve for the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace stays steady with Midnight Call and Candy Warhol not going too fast
scenarios.body: The lack of early burn-up allows closers to conserve energy and unleash their finishing kicks in the final two furlongs. Horses with proven late pace like Dark Sun and Twirler can time their runs perfectly behind the modest early gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runners stay there
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Call maintains her recent AW form and gets an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: With limited early pressure, she can dictate terms and potentially have enough left to resist late challengers. Candy Warhol could also benefit from tracking the leader without being harried early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-race tactical battle
scenarios.trigger: If several hold-up horses converge simultaneously in the final two furlongs creating traffic problems
scenarios.body: The bunching effect allows one horse with a clear run to steal through while others get shuffled back. This chaotic finish could suit whoever gets the clearest passage rather than the best horse on paper.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If both Midnight Call and Candy Warhol go too slow early and get swamped
scenarios.body: The sprint finish becomes a pure speed test over the final furlong, potentially suiting horses with natural pace who don't need the run. Even prominent runners could get caught out by the sudden injection of pace.
